In these Terms of Reference the following terms shall have the following 
meanings: Board shall mean the Board of Directors of the Company; and 
Committee shall mean the Audit and Risk Committee. 
Committee Terms of Reference
1.1
These Terms of Reference have been produced to identify and formalise the 
roles, tasks and responsibilities of the Committee for compliance with the 
UK Corporate Governance Code (the Code), so far as it is appropriate, and to 
assist the Committee in achieving best practice in corporate governance for 
the Company and its subsidiaries (the Group). 
1.2
The Committee has the delegated authority of the Board in respect of the 
functions and powers set out in these Terms of Reference. 
2.1
The Committee shall comprise at least three directors appointed by the 
Board on the recommendation of the Company's Nomination Committee 
in consultation with the chair of the Committee (other than in respect of 
the initial members of the Committee as set out in paragraph 2.2  below). All 
members of the Committee shall be independent non-executive directors 
of the Company. At least one member of the Committee shall have recent 
and relevant financial experience with competence in accounting and/or 
auditing.  The Committee shall include at least, where possible, one member 
of the Remuneration Committee. All the members of the Committee shall 
have competence relevant to the sector in which the Company operates.
2.2
The current members of the Committee are Maurice Horan, Richard 
Stockdale and David Weinreb.

2.3
The Board shall appoint the Committee chair who shall be an independent 
non-executive director. The first chair of the Committee shall be Maurice 
Horan. In the absence of the Committee chair and/or an appointed deputy, 
the remaining members present shall elect one of their number to chair any 
meeting of the Committee. The chair of the Board, where possible, should 
not be a member of the Committee. 
2.4
Only members of the Committee shall have the right to attend and vote 
at Committee meetings. However, the Company's Chief Financial Officer 
(CFO), the Chief Internal Audit Officer and external audit lead partner will 
be invited to attend meetings of the Committee on a regular basis. Other 
individuals, including but not limited to the Board chair, the Chief Executive 
Officer (CEO), the Director of Compliance and Risk, and representatives 
from the finance function of the Company may be invited to attend for all or 
part of any meeting as and when appropriate and necessary. 
3.1
An external service provider duly appointed by the Board as Company 
Secretary (the Company Secretary) shall act as the secretary of the 
Committee (Secretary) and will ensure that the Committee receives 
information and papers in a timely manner to enable full and proper 
consideration to be given to issues contained in them. 
3.2
The Secretary shall also act as a co-ordinating intermediary between the 
Board and the Committee.

4.1
The quorum necessary for the meeting to be convened shall be at least two 
members including, wherever possible, at least one member with recent 
and relevant financial experience and competence in accounting and/or 
auditing, present in person or by telephone, audio or video conference or 
such other electronic facility as provides an electronic means of attendance 
and participation in the meeting to enable all participants to hear one another 
and to be able to communicate with one another. 
4.2
A duly convened Committee meeting at which a quorum is present shall be 
competent to exercise all or any of the authorities, powers and discretions 
vested in or exercisable by the Committee. 
4.3
Resolutions of the Audit and Risk Committee shall require the approval of 
a majority of the members present at a duly convened meeting. Where 
only two (2) members are present, resolutions shall require the unanimous 
agreement of both members.

5.1
The Committee shall meet at least three times a year at appropriate intervals 
in the financial reporting and audit cycle and otherwise as required. 
5.2
Outside of the formal meeting programme, the Committee chair and, to a 
lesser extent the other Committee members, will maintain a dialogue with 
key individuals involved in the Company's governance, including the Chair 
of the Board, the Company's CEO or CFO, the external audit lead partner and 
the Chief Internal Audit Officer (CIAO).

NOTICE OF MEETINGS & 
PROCEEDINGS AT MEETINGS 
06
6.1
Meetings of the Committee shall be called by the Secretary at the request 
of the Committee chair or any of its members or at the request of the CFO 
or the Director of Compliance and Risk or at the request of the Company's 
external audit lead partner or CIAO if they consider it necessary. 
6.2
Unless otherwise agreed, notice of each meeting confirming the venue, 
time and date together with an agenda of items to be discussed, shall be 
circulated to each member of the Committee and any other person required 
to attend, no later than five working days prior to the date of the meeting but 
Committee papers may be forwarded at shorter notice with the approval 
of the Committee chair. Supporting papers shall be sent to Committee 
members and to other attendees as appropriate, at the same time. 
6.3
Notices, agendas and supporting papers can be sent in electronic form.
6.4
All documentation will be prepared to the highest standards of confidentiality 
to protect the security of the information.
6.5
Meetings of the Committee may be conducted when the members are 
physically present or in the form of video or audio conferences or some other 
electronic means enabling attendance and participation in the meeting.
6.6
A resolution in writing and signed by all Committee members will be as 
effective as a resolution passed at a Committee meeting. Any written 
resolution shall be tabled and noted at the next meeting of the Committee. 
6.7
Each Committee member shall have one vote which may be cast on matters 
considered at the meeting. Votes can only be cast by members attending a 
Committee meeting (whether in person or by audio or video conference).
Committee Terms of Reference

6.8
If a matter that is considered by the Committee is one where a Committee 
member, either directly or indirectly, has a personal interest, that member 
shall not be permitted to: (i) receive the relevant information, (ii) attend any 
discussions on the matter, (iii) vote on the matter.
6.9
Except where(i) they have a personal interest, or (ii) the quorum is less than 
3, the Committee chair shall have a casting vote.
6.10
The Committee chair may ask any attendees of a Committee meeting to 
leave the meeting to allow discussions of matters relating to them.

7.1
The Secretary shall minute the proceedings and decisions of all Committee 
meetings (including the names of those present and in attendance). 
7.2
The Secretary should ascertain, at the beginning of each meeting, the 
existence of any conflicts of interest, or any personal financial interest 
(other than as a shareholder) in any matter to be decided on, or any other 
matter which may compromise independence as a non-executive director 
and minute them accordingly.
7.3
Draft minutes of Committee meetings shall be agreed with the Committee 
chair and then circulated promptly to all members of the Committee.

9.1
The Committee should have oversight of the Group as a whole and, 
unless required otherwise by regulation, carry out the duties below for the 
Company's major subsidiary undertakings and the group as a whole.
9.2
The Committee shall, in conducting all of its duties in accordance with 
these Terms of Reference, act in a way it considers in good faith, would be 
most likely to promote the success of the Company for the benefit of its 
members as a whole. In doing so, the Committee must have regard (among 
other matters) to: 
a. the likely consequences of any decision in the long term; 
b. the interests of the Company's employees; 
c. the need to foster the Company's business relationships with suppliers, 
customers and others; 
d. the impact of the Company's operations on the community and the 
environment; 
e. the desirability of the Company maintaining a reputation for high 
standards of business conduct; and 
f. the need to act fairly with all members of the Company.
Policies 
g. The Committee shall review, amend and approve policies that have 
board-level governance, regulatory or statutory implications and have 
been delegated by the Board for the Committee’s approval. 
Financial Reporting
9.3
The Committee shall monitor the integrity of the financial statements of the 
Company, including its annual and half-yearly reports and any other formal 
announcements relating to its financial performance, and review and report 
to the Board on significant financial reporting issues and judgements which 
those statements or announcements contain having regard to matters 
communicated to it by the auditor.

9.4
In particular, the Committee shall review and challenge where necessary:
a. the application of significant accounting policies and any changes to 
them; 
b. the methods used to account for significant or unusual transactions 
where different approaches are possible;
c. whether the Group has followed appropriate accounting policies and 
made appropriate estimates and judgements taking into account the 
views of the external auditor on the financial statements; 
d. all material information presented with the financial statements, 
including the strategic review and the corporate governance statements 
relating to the audit and risk management; 
e. the clarity and completeness of disclosures in the Group's financial 
reports and any changes to these disclosures, and the context in which 
statements are made, including the review of any correspondence 
between the Company and the external auditor; 
f. significant adjustments resulting from the external audit;  
g. the assumptions or qualifications in support of the going concern 
statement (including consideration of any material uncertainties as 
to the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern over a period 
of at least twelve months from the date of approval of the financial 
statements); and  
h. whether it is appropriate for the Board to give its longer term viability 
statement (including an assessment of the prospects of the Company 
and the Group looking forward over an appropriate and justified period). 
9.5
For any other statements containing financial information that require Board 
approval, the Committee will carry out a prior review where practicable 
and consistent with any prompt reporting requirements under any law or 
regulation. 
9.6
Where the Committee is not satisfied with any aspect of the proposed 
financial reporting by the Group, it shall report its views to the Board. 
9.7
The Committee shall monitor and review the tax strategy of the Group and 
any significant tax issues affecting it at least once a year. 
9.8
The Committee shall evaluate, at least annually, the risks to the quality and 
effectiveness of the financial reporting process and consider the need to 
include the risk of the withdrawal of the auditor from the market in that 
evaluation.

Narrative reporting
9.9
Where requested by the Board, the Committee shall review the content of 
the annual report and accounts and advise the Board on whether, taken as a 
whole, it is fair, balanced and understandable and provides the information 
necessary for shareholders to assess the Company's position, performance, 
business model and strategy, and whether it informs the Board’s statement 
in the annual report on these matters that is required under the Code.
Risk appetite, tolerance and strategy
9.10
The Committee shall: 
a. advise the Board on the Company’s overall risk appetite, tolerance and 
strategy, and the principal and emerging risks, including any material 
Environment, Social and Corporate Governance (ESG) related risks, that 
the Company is willing to take in order to achieve its long-term strategic 
objectives; 
b. factor in material ESG-related risks and opportunities - which include 
human rights and climate-related risks - when reviewing annual budgets 
and business plans as well as setting the organization’s performance 
objectives, monitoring implementation and performance, and 
overseeing major capital expenditures, acquisitions, and divestitures; 
c. seek assurance on the risks the Company identifies as those to which 
the business may be exposed; 
d. advise the Board on the likelihood and the impact of principal risks 
materialising, and the management and mitigation of principal risks to 
reduce the likelihood of their incidence or their impact; and  
e. advise the Board on the risk aspects of proposed changes to strategy and 
strategic transactions including acquisitions or disposals, ensuring that 
a due diligence appraisal of the proposition is undertaken, focussing in 
particular on implications for the risk appetite, tolerance and strategy of 
the Company, and taking independent external advice where appropriate 
and available.

Internal Controls and Risk Management Systems
9.11
The Committee shall keep under review the Company’s internal financial 
controls and internal control and risk management systems that identify, 
assess, manage and monitor financial risks, and other integral control and 
risk management systems, and review and approve the statements to be 
included in the annual report concerning internal control, risk management 
and the viability statement, including: 
a. reviewing the Company’s procedures to manage or mitigate principal 
risks including any material ESG-related risks, and to identify emerging 
risks, to assist in the Board’s assessment of principal and emerging risks; 
b. reviewing and assessing the Company’s risk appetite and any associated 
stress testing; 
c. evaluating the Company’s principal risks, including material climate-
related risks and opportunities, to be taken into account by the Board 
when assessing the Company’s prospects; 
d. overseeing the Company’s ability to reduce the likelihood and/or impact 
of principal risks materialising; 
e. ensuring risk management policies take into consideration management 
of material ESG-related risks and opportunities; 
f. overseeing and holding Management accountable in determining 
ESG-related metrics, establishing baseline, transition plans and setting 
targets as applicable; 
g. overseeing the appropriateness of the Company’s values and culture 
and reward systems for managing risk and internal controls, and the 
extent to which the culture and values are embedded at all levels of the 
Company; and  
h. overseeing the Director of Compliance and Risk’s right of direct access 
to the chair of the Committee.

9.12
The Committee shall monitor the Company's internal financial controls, all 
other material internal operating and compliance controls, risk management 
systems, and the effectiveness of its internal audit function. In doing so, 
the Committee shall assist the Board in monitoring and reviewing the 
effectiveness of the Company's risk management and internal control 
framework (including its financial, reporting, operational and compliance 
controls) and draw on the results of the ongoing monitoring process to 
obtain sound, appropriately documented evidence to support the relevant 
statements and confirmations required from the Board in the annual report 
(and, in the case of (f) below, the half-yearly financial statements including: 
a. that the Board has carried out a robust assessment of the emerging 
and principal risks facing the Company, including those that would 
threaten its business model, future performance, solvency or liquidity 
and the Board's description of those principal risks, its description of 
the procedures in place to identify emerging risks and its explanation of 
how they are being managed or mitigated; 
b. taking into account the Company's current position and principal risks, 
how the Board has assessed the prospects of the Company, over what 
period it has done so and why it considers that period to be appropriate; 
c. whether the Board has a reasonable expectation that the Company will 
be able to continue in operation and meet its liabilities as they fall due 
over the period of its assessment, drawing attention to any qualifications 
or assumptions as necessary; 
d. an explanation of how the Board has reviewed the effectiveness, at 
least annually, of the Company's risk management and internal control 
framework (including its financial, operational and compliance controls) 
and the Board's report on that review;  
e. a declaration on the effectiveness of material controls as of the balance 
sheet date, and a description of any material controls that have not 
operated effectively and action taken or planned to improve them1;
f. the appropriateness of adopting the going concern basis of accounting 
in the financial statements and whether there are any material 
uncertainties to the Company's ability to continue to do so over a period 
of at least twelve months from the date of the approval of the financial 
statements. 
9.13
The Committee shall oversee and advise the Board on the Company’s and 
the Group’s current risk exposure and future risk strategy and annually 
consider how the remuneration of executives shapes their view of risk.
Committee Terms of Reference

9.14
The Committee shall review the timeliness of, and reports on, the 
effectiveness of corrective action taken by management in response to any 
material external or internal audit recommendation.
9.15
The Committee shall consider any necessary disclosure implications of the 
process that has been applied by the Board to deal with material internal 
control aspects of any significant problems disclosed in the annual report 
and accounts.
9.16
The Committee shall consider the major findings of any relevant internal 
investigations into risk and control weaknesses, fraud or misconduct and 
management’s response, and also consider whether any such failings or 
weaknesses are significant and therefore require disclosure, the basis and 
accuracy of explanations given as to what actions are being taken to address 
them, and whether the level of disclosure of such actions is appropriate. 
Compliance, whistleblowing and fraud 
9.17
The Committee shall review the adequacy and security of the Company's 
Group's arrangements for its employees, contractors and other members of 
its workforce to raise concerns, in confidence, about possible wrongdoing 
in financial reporting or other matters. The Committee shall ensure that 
these arrangements allow proportionate and independent investigation of 
such matters and appropriate follow up action. The Committee shall also 
review the Company's Group's procedures for detecting fraud, review the 
Company's Group's systems and controls for the prevention of bribery, 
money-laundering and receive reports on non-compliance. 
9.18
The Committee shall review regular reports from the Compliance Officer 
and the adequacy and effectiveness the company's anti-money laundering 
systems and controls. It shall also review regular reports from the 
Compliance Officer and keep under review the adequacy and effectiveness 
of the Company's compliance functions. 
Committee Terms of Reference

Internal Audit 
9.19
The company has an internal audit function which is commensurate with 
the size of the business and complexity of the operations carried out. The 
Committee shall: 
a. approve the appointment or termination of appointment of the Head of 
Internal Audit; 
b. review and approve the role and mandate of internal audit, monitor and 
review the effectiveness of its work, and annually approve the internal 
audit charter ensuring it is appropriate for the current needs of the 
organisation; 
c. review and approve the annual internal audit plan to ensure it is aligned 
to the key risks of the business, and receive regular reports on work 
carried out; 
d. ensure internal audit has unrestricted scope, the necessary resources 
and access to information to enable it to fulfil its mandate, ensure 
there is open communication between different functions and that the 
internal audit function evaluates the effectiveness of these functions as 
part of its internal audit plan, and ensure that the internal audit function 
is equipped to perform in accordance with appropriate professional 
standards for internal auditors; 
e. ensure the internal auditor has direct access to the Board chair and to 
the Committee chair, providing independence from the executive and 
accountability to the Committee; 
f. carry out an annual assessment of the effectiveness of the internal 
audit function, and as part of this assessment: 
i. meet with the head of internal audit without the presence of 
management to discuss the effectiveness of the function; 
ii. review and assess the annual internal audit work plan; 
iii. receive a report on the results of the internal auditor’s work; 
iv. determine whether it is satisfied that the quality, experience and 
expertise of internal audit is appropriate for the business; and 
v. review the actions taken by management to implement the 
recommendations of internal audit and to support the effective working 
of the internal audit function 
f. monitor and assess the role and effectiveness of the internal audit 
function in the overall context of the Company’s risk management 
system and the work of compliance, finance and the external auditor;
g. consider whether an independent, third party review of process is 
appropriate;

External Audit
9.20
The Committee shall consider and make recommendations to the Board, 
to be put to shareholders for approval at the Company's Annual General 
Meeting, as regards the appointment, re-appointment and removal of the 
Company's external auditor.
9.21
The Committee shall develop and lead the selection process for the 
appointment of the external audit firm, ensuring that all tendering firms have 
access to all necessary information and individuals during the tendering 
process. All members of the Committee should be involved throughout the 
tender process.
9.22
The Committee will take account of the need to expand market diversity 
and any market opening measures that may be introduced. In particular, the 
Committee must carry out the selection procedures in accordance with 
Article 16(3) of the Audit Regulation, which states that the tender process 
must not in any way preclude the participation of firms which received less 
than 15 % of the total audit fees from public interest entities in the previous 
calendar year.
9.23
The choice of auditor should be based on quality, including independence, 
challenge and technical competence, not price or perceived cultural fit. The 
audit committee should consider running a price-blind audit tender.
9.24
The Committee will communicate with any eligible audit firms that are 
unwilling to tender to: 
a. understand why they are unwilling to tender and whether there is 
anything that could be done to change that; 
b. ask how such action is in the public interest; and 
c. remind them that they may as a result be ineligible to bid for non-audit 
services work. 
9.25
If an external auditor resigns, the Committee shall investigate the issues 
leading to this and decide whether any action is required.
Committee Terms of Reference

9.26
The Committee shall oversee the relationship with the 
external auditor and shall: 
a. negotiate and approve their remuneration, including both fees for audit 
and non-audit services, and ensure that the level of fees is appropriate 
to enable an effective and high quality audit to be conducted; 
b. approve their terms of engagement, including any engagement letter 
issued at the start of each audit and the scope of the audit; 
c. ensure that the external auditor has full access to the Company’s 
employees and records; 
d. assess annually the external auditor’s independence and objectivity 
taking into account relevant UK law, regulation, the Financial Reporting 
Council’s Ethical Standard (FRC's Ethical Standard) and other 
professional requirements and the Group relationship with the auditor 
as a whole, including any threats to the auditor’s independence and the 
safeguards applied to mitigate those threats including the provision of 
any non-audit services; 
e. satisfy itself that there are no relationships (such as family, employment, 
investment, financial or business) between the external auditor and the 
Company (other than in the ordinary course of business) which could 
adversely affect the external auditor's independence and objectivity; 
f. agree with the Board a policy on the employment of former employees 
of the Company's external auditor, taking into account the FRC’s Ethical 
Standard and legal requirements, and monitor the implementation of 
that policy, in particular relating to former employees who were part of 
the audit team and moved directly to the company; 
g. monitor the auditor’s processes for maintaining independence, its 
compliance with relevant UK law, regulations, other professional 
requirements and the FRC’s Ethical Standard, including the guidance on 
the rotation of audit partners and staff; 
h. monitor the level of fees paid by the Company to the external auditor 
compared to the overall fee income of the firm, office and partner and 
assess these in the context of relevant legal, professional and regulatory 
requirements, guidance and the FRC’s Ethical Standard; 
i. assess annual the qualifications, expertise and resources, and 
independence of the external auditor and the effectiveness of the 
external audit process, which shall include a report from the external 
auditor on their own internal quality procedures; 
j. seek to ensure co-ordination of the external audit with the activities of 
the internal audit function; 
k. evaluate the risks to the quality and effectiveness of the financial 
reporting process in light of the external auditor’s communications with 
the Committee. 
Committee Terms of Reference

9.27
The Committee shall develop and recommend to the Board the Company’s 
formal policy on the provision of audit and non-audit services by the 
auditor, including prior approval of non-audit services by the Committee 
and specifying the types of non-audit services to be pre-approved, and 
assessment of whether non-audit services have a direct or material effect 
on the audited financial statements.  The policy should include consideration 
of the following matters: 
a. threats to the independence and objectivity of the external auditor and 
any safeguards in place, taking into account relevant UK law, regulation, 
the FRC’s Ethical Standard and other professional requirements; 
b. the nature of the non-audit services; 
c. whether the external audit firm is the most suitable supplier of the non-
audit service; 
d. the fees for the non-audit services, both individually and in aggregate, 
relative to the audit fee; and 
e. the criteria governing compensation; 
f. annual review of relationships between the Company and various audit 
firms for non-audit work to ensure that there is a fair choice of suitable 
external auditors at the next tender. 
9.28
The Committee shall meet regularly with the external auditor (including 
once at the planning stage before the audit and once after the audit at the 
reporting stage) and, at least once a year, meet with the external auditor 
without management being present to discuss the auditor’s remit and any 
issues arising from the audit.
9.29
The Committee shall discuss with the external auditor the factors that could 
affect audit quality and review and approve the annual audit plan, ensuring 
it is consistent with the scope of the audit engagement, having regard to the 
seniority, expertise and experience of the audit team;
9.30
The Committee shall review the findings of the audit with the external 
auditor.  This shall include but not be limited to, the following: 
a. a discussion of any major issues which arose during the audit; 
b. the auditor’s explanation of how the risks to audit quality were addressed; 
c. key accounting and audit judgements; 
d. the auditor’s view of their interactions with senior management; and 
e. levels of errors identified during the audit. 
Committee Terms of Reference

9.31
The Committee shall review any representation letter(s) requested by the 
external auditor before they are signed by management.
9.32
The Committee shall review the management letter and management’s 
response to the auditor’s findings and recommendations. 
9.33
The Committee shall review the effectiveness of the audit process taking 
into account relevant UK law, regulation, the FRC’s Ethical Standard and 
other professional requirements, including an assessment of the quality of 
the audit, the handling of key judgements by the auditor, and the auditor’s 
response to the questions from the Committee.
10.1
The Committee chair shall report formally to the Board on its proceedings 
after each meeting on all matters within its duties and responsibilities 
and shall also formally report to the Board on how it has discharged its 
responsibilities. This report shall include: 
a. the significant issues that it considered in relation to the financial 
statements (required under paragraph The Committee shall monitor 
the integrity of the financial statements of the Company, including its 
annual and half-yearly reports and any other formal announcements 
relating to its financial performance, and review and report to the 
Board on significant financial reporting issues and judgements which 
those statements or announcements contain having regard to matters 
communicated to it by the auditor.) and how these were addressed; 
b. its assessment of the effectiveness of the external audit process 
(required under paragraph The Committee shall review the effectiveness 
of the audit process taking into account relevant UK law, regulation, the 
FRC’s Ethical Standard and other professional requirements, including an 
assessment of the quality of the audit, the handling of key judgements 
by the auditor, and the auditor’s response to the questions from the 
Committee), the approach taken to the appointment or reappointment 
of the external auditor, length of tenure of the external audit firm, when a 
tender was last conducted and advance notice of any retendering plans; 
c. any other issues on which the Board has requested the Committee's 
opinion.

RESPONSIBILITIES 
Committee Terms of Reference

10.2
The Committee shall make whatever recommendations to the Board it 
deems appropriate on any area within its remit where action or improvement 
is needed. 
10.3
The Committee shall compile a report on its activities to be included in the 
Company's annual report. The Committee's report shall include: 
a. the significant issues the Committee considered in relation to the 
financial statements and how these issues were addressed; 
b. an explanation of the application of the entity’s accounting policies; 
c. where shareholders have requested that certain matters be covered 
in an audit and that request has been rejected, an explanation of the 
reasons why; 
d. where a regulatory inspection of the quality of the company’s audit has 
taken place, information about the findings of that review, together with 
any remedial action the auditor is taking in the light of these findings; 
e. an explanation of how the Committee has assessed the independence 
and effectiveness of the external audit process, the approach taken to 
the appointment or reappointment of the eternal auditor, information 
on the length of tenure of the current audit firm, when a tender was last 
conducted and advance notice of any retendering plans; 
f. in the case of the Board not accepting the Committee's recommendation 
on the external auditor appointment, reappointment or removal, a 
statement from the Committee explaining its recommendation and the 
reasons why the Board has taken a different position; 
g. the criteria used and the tender process followed to make the selection 
of an external auditor; 
h. an explanation of how auditor independence and objectivity are 
safeguarded if the external auditor provides non-audit services, having 
regard to matters communicated to it by the auditor and all other 
information requirements set out in the Code;  
i. the activities undertaken to meet the requirements of the FRC’s Audit 
Committees and the External Audit  Minimum Standard; and 
j. any other issues on which the Board has requested the Committee’s

Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement
Page 3
This statement is made pursuant to Section 54 of the Modern Slavery 
Act 2015 (the “Act”) and sets out Dar Global’s commitment to preventing 
slavery and human trafficking in our own business and our supply chains. 
Our employees are already aware, through our Code of Conduct, of our zero-
tolerance stance against any form of modern slavery, including forced child 
labour. We also have Whistleblowing channels available which they may use 
to report any concerns to Dar Global’s management. 
Dar Global Plc is an international property developer operating in Europe 
(United Kingdom, Spain and Greece), the Americas (the United States) 
and the Middle East and Asia (the UAE, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the 
Maldives). Each region has its own management structure, supported by, 
and reporting into the Group Head Office located in Dubai, UAE. 
Dar Global’s supply chain is comprised of hundreds of third-party suppliers, 
contractors and subcontractors on whom we rely on to execute our 
development projects through the supply of goods and services. 
 
Procurement of these third-party goods and services is dealt with by each of 
the regional divisions. Due diligence as to the third parties’ compliance with 
Dar Global’s policies and procedures is managed by a central team based at 
Head Office and is a continuous process.  
01 
02
OVERVIEW OF OUR 
ORGANISATIONAL 
STRUCTURE 
SUPPLY CHAIN
Dar Global – Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement 2026

Page 4
Some of Dar Global’s suppliers, contractors and subcontractors are smaller 
businesses, others are located in jurisdictions where labour protections, 
enforcement mechanisms or anti-slavery regulations may be less developed. 
Dar Global recognises that these entities, along with their suppliers and 
subcontractors, present the most risk to its business in relation to the 
Act, and aims to tailor its responses to local circumstances. As part of our 
onboarding and ongoing monitoring processes, suppliers and contractors 
may be subject to risk-based due diligence, including sanctions screening, 
beneficial ownership checks and reviews of compliance with applicable 
laws and ethical standards 
We recognise our moral and ethical responsibilities to do all we can to 
ensure that our business and supply chains are slavery free. In order to 
help achieve this we maintain a number of internal policies, including our 
Whistleblowing Policy, Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy and Code of 
Conduct, which support our commitment to preventing modern slavery and 
protecting human rights.. The internal policies include Whistleblowing, Anti-
Bribery and Corruption, and our Code of Conduct that covers our approach 
to Harassment and Bullying, Diversity and Modern Slavery. 
 
Dar Global’s Group companies and subsidiaries operating in the Middle 
Eastoperate with integrity and uphold high standards of ethical conduct and 
human rights. While not subject to the UK Modern Slavery Act, our affiliated 
Middle East companies fully comply with local labour and anti-trafficking 
laws. 
03
04
HIGH RISK AREAS 
DAR GLOBAL’S POLICIES 
Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement
Dar Global – Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement 2026

Page 5
Contract terms 
Dar Global’s standard contractor and supplier terms include an obligation 
on contractors and suppliers to obtain similar commitments from their 
subcontractors and suppliers. 
Dar Global prohibits all forms of forced labour, modern slavery, and human 
trafficking within its operations and supply chain. We have provisions in our 
contracts for our projects in the Middle East and Asia region that obligates 
contractors to comply with local labour laws; these cover employment, 
health, safety and welfare, immigration and emigration. Further, contractors 
are obligated to pay their employees at least the national minimum wages, 
or no lower than those established as per the trade or industry standard (as 
appropriate). 
  
We have set minimum welfare standards for our contractors’ on-site staff 
and labour. 
 
Training and awareness 
Dar Global provides training and awareness materials to all its employees 
for them to understand the signs of modern slavery and what to do if they 
suspect it is taking place. Refresher training will take place at regular intervals. 
Performance Indicators
We will assess the effectiveness of the steps being taken to ensure 
thatmodern slavery and human trafficking are not taking place in our 
business or supply chains by monitoring: 
• Any reports or concerns raised by employees, contractors, suppliers, 
members of the public or law enforcement agencies relating to modern 
slavery or human trafficking; and;  
Any identified instances of non-compliance by suppliers or contractors 
with applicable labour laws or contractual obligations relating to ethical 
employment practices.To date, no reports have been received, but this may 
change as the company raises further awareness of the Modern Slavery Act. 
To date, no reports or identified instances of modern slavery have been 
brought to the Company's attention.
05  ACTIONS TAKEN TO 
COMBAT MODERN SLAVERY

Dar Global – Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement 2026

Page 6
Dar Global – Anti-slavery & human trafficking Statement 2026 
Further steps to be undertaken 
The company will continue to assess higher-risk suppliers and may require 
certain suppliers to provide annual modern slavery statements or equivalent 
confirmations regarding their compliance programmes.

17th June 2026. 
This statement was approved by the Board of Dar Global Plc on 
24th June 2026. 
 
David Weinreb  
Chairman

DarGlobal is committed to respecting your privacy and complying with 
applicable data protection and privacy laws. You can visit https://www.
darglobal.co.uk without disclosing your identity information, if you prefer. 
Please note that, when purchasing a unit, it is essential that you provide 
certain personal information upon request; otherwise, we may be unable 
to complete the transaction. In most other circumstances, choosing not to 
share your personal data will not have negative consequences and you will 
still be able to browse our website, explore property listings, verify corporate 
information and access brochures online. If some personal information is 
withheld by you, we may be limited in our ability to contact you or carry out 
specific actions you request, as certain details are necessary to respond to 
enquiries or process your instructions.
DarGlobal consists of a number of distinct companies, each handling 
particular developments and associated services (jointly referred to as 
“Group”). These may change over time as our land portfolio and property 
offerings expand or evolve. Whenever you express interest in a specific 
development, the company that promotes that development – which 
may, sometimes, include companies that are partners of DarGlobal and 
do not belong to the Group – and Group entities which are responsible for 
administrative activities will manage the use of your personal data.
This Privacy Policy will help you understand how we collect, use, and protect 
your personal information.
This policy should be read in conjunction with the Terms and Conditions 
section of this site.

STATEMENT

Acceptance
By using this site and/or providing us your personal data by any means, you 
agree with this Privacy Policy. DarGlobal is committed to conducting its 
business in full compliance with all applicable data protection and privacy 
laws. We respect the rights and expectations of our customers and other 
individuals whose data we process, and we handle personal information 
responsibly, lawfully, and with integrity. Our aim is to ensure transparency, 
safeguard personal data, and maintain the trust placed in us.
What personal information may be collected and processed? 
You may have to disclose certain personal information with us to use our 
services. We may collect and process some or  all of the following personal 
data from you when you enter  (or intend to) enter into a business relationship 
with us:
• name

manage your subscription and keep you informed about updates, services,

relevant to you.

The information provided in this form will be used to reserve the concerned 
property upon customer request and process the purchase. Furthermore, 
DarGlobal is required to comply with anti-money laundering regulations in 
certain jurisdictions where it operates, and some of the information provided 
may be processed for that purpose.
Page 4
Data Privacy Statement
Dar Global – Data Privacy Statement 2026

Cookies and Other Tracking Technologies
We may collect personal information from you when you use, including but 
not limited to, the contact options and e-mail. In addition to the personal 
information we collect, the website server will automatically recognize and 
store your internet address. In addition, this website may use cookies. A 
cookie is a small text file which is placed onto your computer (or another 
electronic device) when you use our website. Most web browsers are set 
by default to accept cookies; however, you may set your browser to either 
accept or refuse cookies. Cookies help websites keep track of personal 
preferences and recognize return visitors. The cookies are not designed to 
collect or store information on you, but to deliver targeted content to you
online.
DarGlobal retains personal data only as long as necessary to fulfil the 
specified purposes or comply with applicable laws. Retention periods are 
determined by:
• Contractual obligations
• Legal requirements
• Business needs
Personal data no longer needed will be securely deleted or anonymized.
How safe will my personal information be?
The security of all information associated with our customers is a very 
important concern to us. Therefore, at DarGlobal, we exercise the utmost 
care in providing secure transmission of your information from your own 
device to our servers. As known, no data transmission over the Internet can 
be guaranteed to be 100% secure. As a result, while we strive to protect 
your information, DarGlobal cannot ensure or warrant the security of any 
information you transmit to us, or from our online products or services, 
and you do so at your risk. Once we receive your transmission, DarGlobal 
uses industry standard efforts to safeguard the confidentiality of your 
information.
Page 5
Data Privacy Statement
Dar Global – Data Privacy Statement 2026

Who will have access to my personal information?
The general rule is that DarGlobal will not disclose any personal information 
that you submit to us in a manner that it would link to your identity, except 
when we have your explicit permission to disclose it, or under special 
circumstances, such as when we believe in good faith that the nature of our 
relationship or the law requires it.
We may share your personal information with trusted third parties, including 
service providers, agents, subcontractors, and other organisations that 
support us in delivering services either to our company or directly
to you. These parties may include IT providers (such as website hosting and 
software for administrative purposes), research firms conducting surveys or 
feedback on our behalf, DarGlobal partners which may be part of your Sales 
and Purchase Agreement, companies that are party to joint ventures with 
DarGlobal for the development you purchased or intend to purchase, utility 
suppliers for your purchased property, as well as your appointed solicitors or 
other authorised representatives, introducers, or professional advisors.
We may also share your personal information with regulatory and government 
agencies, if and when DarGlobal is required to do so by law or Court order.
When we use data processors to process your personal data on our behalf, we 
will retain control over and we will remain fully responsible for your personal 
data and we will use appropriate safeguards as required by applicable law to 
ensure the integrity and security of your personal data when engaging such 
service providers.
For what purposes is my personal information collected and processed?
Personal data is collected and processed by DarGlobal for the following 
purposes:
• To provide and manage services and products requested
         by customers
• To respond to inquiries and service requests
• To send updates about projects, products, or services
• To follow up on clients about our services and products
• To process property reservations or related transactions
• To comply with legal requirements
• To perform a contract
• For legitimate business needs, such as statistical
         analysis and historical reporting

Dar Global – Data Privacy Statement 2026

What is the legal basis for DarGlobal to process my personal information?
DarGlobal processes personal data lawfully and fairly, relying on the following 
legal grounds:
• Consent provided explicitly by data subject
• Necessity for the performance of a contract
• Compliance with legal obligations
• Protection of vital interests of the data subject
• Legitimate business interests, provided they do not
        override data subject rights; and
• The purpose for collecting and processing personal

        the legal basis for processing is communicated to the
        data subject.

By post: Compliance Department, Media One Tower Level 35, Dubai Media 
City, Al Falak St. Exit 32, PO Box 2523, Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

by default to accept cookies; however, you may set your browser to either 
accept or refuse cookies. Cookies help websites keep track of personal 
preferences and recognize return visitors. The cookies are not designed to 
collect or store information on you, but to deliver targeted content to you
online.

specified purposes or comply with applicable laws. Retention periods are 
determined by:

• Legal requirements
• Business needs

important concern to us. Therefore, at DarGlobal, we exercise the utmost 
care in providing secure transmission of your information from your own 
device to our servers. As known, no data transmission over the Internet can 
be guaranteed to be 100% secure. As a result, while we strive to protect 
your information, DarGlobal cannot ensure or warrant the security of any 
information you transmit to us, or from our online products or services, 
and you do so at your risk. Once we receive your transmission, DarGlobal 
uses industry standard efforts to safeguard the confidentiality of your 
information.

circumstances, such as when we believe in good faith that the nature of our

subsidiary undertakings and the Group as a whole, as appropriate.

knowledge, independence, experience, length of service and diversity) 
of the Board as a whole and make recommendations to the Board with 
regard to any changes; 
b. ensure plans are in place for orderly succession to Board and senior 
management positions, and oversee the development of a diverse 
pipeline for succession, taking into account the challenges and 
opportunities facing the Company, and the skills and expertise needed 
on the Board in the future; 
c. keep under review the leadership needs of the organisation, both 
executive and non-executive, with a view to ensuring the continued 
ability of the organisation to compete effectively in the marketplace; 
d. keep up to date and fully informed about strategic issues and commercial 
changes affecting the Company and the market in which it operates; 
e. be responsible for identifying and nominating for the approval of the 
Board, candidates to fill Board vacancies as and when they arise; 
f. keep under review the Board’s policy on diversity, inclusion and equal 
opportunity; 
g. before any appointment is made by the Board, evaluate the balance 
of skills, knowledge, experience and diversity on the Board, and, in the 
light of this evaluation, prepare a description of the role and capabilities 
required for a particular appointment and the time commitment 
expected. In identifying suitable candidates the Committee shall:
i. use open advertising or the services of external advisers to facilitate the 
search; 
ii.  consider candidates from a wide range of backgrounds;
iii. consider candidates on merit and against objective criteria and with 
due regard for the benefits of diversity on the Board and taking care 
to ensure that appointees have enough time available to devote to the 
position;

expected of them in terms of time commitment, committee service 
and involvement outside Board meetings;
j. review the results of the Board performance evaluation process that 
relate to the composition of the board and succession planning; 
k. review annually the time required from non-executive directors, 
with performance evaluation being used to assess whether the non-
executive directors are spending enough time to fulfil their duties; 
l. work and liaise as necessary with other Board committees, ensuring 
the interaction between committees and with the Board is regularly 
reviewed; and 
m. ensure that all new directors undertake an appropriate induction 
programme to ensure that they are fully informed about strategic and 
commercial issues affecting the Company and the markets in which 
it operates as well as their duties and responsibilities as a director and 
consider any training requirements for the Board as a whole.

a. any changes needed to the succession planning process if its periodic 
assessment indicates the desired outcomes have not been achieved; 
b. suitable candidates as new directors and succession for existing 
directors; 
c. membership of the audit and risk and remuneration committees, and 
any other Board committees as appropriate, in consultation with the 
chair of those committees; 
d. the re-appointment of non-executive directors at the conclusion of their 
specified time of office having given due regard to their performance 
and ability to continue to contribute to the Board in light of knowledge, 
skills and experience required, 
e. the re-election by shareholders of directors under the annual re-
election provisions of the articles of association and the UK Corporate 
Governance Code, having due regard to their performance and ability, 
and why their contribution is important to the Company’s long-term 
sustainable success in the light of the knowledge, skills and experience 
required and the need for progressive refreshing of the Board, taking into 
account the length of service of individual directors, the chair and the 
Board as a whole;
f. any matters relating to the continuation in office of any director at any 
time, including the suspension or termination of service of an executive 
director as an employee of the Company, subject to the provisions of 
the law and their service contract; and 
g. the appointment of any director to executive or other officer.
Committee Terms of Reference
Dar Global – Nomination Committee Terms of Reference June 2026

10.1
The Committee chair shall report to the Board after each meeting on the 
nature and content of its discussions, recommendations and actions to be 
taken. 
10.2
The Committee shall make whatever recommendations to the Board it 
deems appropriate on any area within its remit where action or improvement 
is needed and adequate time should be made available for Board discussion 
when necessary. 
10.3
The Committee shall produce a report to be included in the Company's 
annual report describing the work of the Committee, including:
a. the process used in relation to appointments, its approach to succession 
planning and how both support the development of a diverse pipeline; 
b. how Board evaluation has been conducted, the nature and extent of 
an external evaluator’s contact with the Board and individual directors, 
the outcomes and actions taken, and how the Board evaluation has 
influenced or will influence the Board’s composition; 
c. the policy on diversity and inclusion, its objectives and linkage to the 
Company’s strategy, how it has been implemented and progress on 
achieving the objectives; and 
d. the gender balance of those in the senior management team and their 
direct reports.
10.4
If an external search consultancy has been engaged, it should be identified 
in the Company’s annual report alongside a statement about any other 
connection it has with the Company or individual directors.

RESPONSIBILITIES

11.1
The Committee shall have access to sufficient resources in order to carry 
out its duties, including access to the Company Secretary for advice and 
assistance as required, and be provided   with appropriate and timely training, 
both in the form of an induction programme for new members and on an 
ongoing basis for all members.
11.2
The Committee shall give due consideration to all relevant laws and 
regulations including the general duties of directors in the Companies 
Act 2006, the provisions of the UK Corporate Governance Code and 
associated guidance (so far as it is appropriate), the requirements of the 
Financial Conduct Authority's Listing Rules, Prospectus Regulation Rules 
and Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules sourcebook and any other 
applicable rules, as appropriate. 
11.3
The Committee shall ensure that a periodic evaluation of its own performance 
is carried out and, at least annually, review its constitution and these Terms 
of Reference to ensure it is operating at maximum effectiveness and 
recommend any changes it considers necessary to the Board for approval.
11.4
The Committee shall commission a regular externally facilitated board 
performance review. If the company is part of the FTSE 350, this should 
happen at least every three years. The external reviewer should be identified 
in the annual report and a statement made about any other connection it 
has with the company or individual directors.

consultancies and to commission or purchase any reports, surveys or 
information which it deems necessary.
12.2
The Board authorises the Committee to seek any information it requires 
from any employee or director of the Company, and all such employees 
or directors will be directed to co-operate with any request made by the 
Committee.

Subject to the constitutional documents of the Company, the Committee 
shall determine its own procedures.  
Adopted by the Board June 2026

account of Company and individual performance, and wider circumstances.

should avoid designing pay structures based solely on benchmarking to the

9.1
The Committee shall:
a. have delegated responsibility for determining the policy for directors’ 
remuneration and setting remuneration for the Company’s chair and 
executive directors and senior management (defined as C-Suite1 
employees) or the Board Chair, in accordance with the Principles 
and Provisions of the UK Corporate Governance Code so far as it is 
appropriate, and within the scope of the directors' remuneration policy 
as approved by the Company's shareholders; 
b. have delegated responsibility for setting remuneration for the Company 
Secretary; 
c. establish remuneration schemes that promote long-term shareholding 
by executive directors that support alignment with long-term shareholder 
interests, with share awards subject to a total vesting and holding period 
of at least five years, and a formal policy post- employment shareholding 
requirements encompassing both unvested and vested shares; 
d. design remuneration policies and practices to support strategy and 
promote long-term sustainable success, with executive remuneration 
aligned to Company purpose and values, clearly linked to the successful 
delivery of the Company’s long-term strategy, and that enable the use of 
discretion to override formulaic outcomes and to recover and/or withhold 
sums or share awards under appropriate specified circumstances; and 
e.  when determining executive director remuneration policy and practices, 
consider the UK Corporate Governance Code, so far as it is appropriate, 
requirements for clarity, simplicity, risk mitigation, predictability, 
proportionality and alignment to culture. 
9.2
No director or senior manager shall be involved in any decisions as to their 
own remuneration outcome. The Board itself or, where required by the 
Articles of Association or other constitutional documents of the Company, 
the shareholders should determine the remuneration of the non- executive 
directors within the limits set out in those Articles of Association or other 
constitutional documents.

9.3
In determining remuneration policy, the Committee shall take into account 
all other factors which it deems necessary, including relevant legal and 
regulatory requirements, the provisions and recommendations of the 
UK Corporate Governance Code and associated guidance (so far as it is 
appropriate). The objective of such remuneration policy shall be to attract, 
retain and motivate executive management of the quality required to run 
the Company successfully without paying more than is necessary, having 
regard to views of shareholders and other stakeholders.
9.4
The Committee shall review the ongoing appropriateness and relevance of 
the Company’s remuneration policy. 
9.5
Within the terms of the agreed policy and in consultation with the chair and/
or chief executive, as appropriate, the Committee shall determine the total 
individual remuneration package of each executive director, the Company 
chair and senior managers, including bonuses, incentive payments and 
share options or other share awards. The choice of financial, non-financial 
and strategic measures is important, as is the exercise of independent 
judgement and discretion when determining remuneration awards, taking 
account of Company and individual performance, and wider circumstances. 
9.6
The Committee shall have full authority to appoint remuneration consultants 
and to commission or purchase any reports, surveys or information which it 
seems necessary at the expense of the Company. However, the Committee 
should avoid designing pay structures based solely on benchmarking to the 
market or on the advice of remuneration consultants.
9.7
The Committee shall review the design of all share incentive plans for 
approval by the Board and, where required, shareholders. For any such plans, 
the Committee shall determine each year whether awards will be made 
and, the overall amount of such awards, the individual awards for executive 
directors and senior managers and the performance targets to be used. 
9.8
The Committee shall review workforce remuneration and related policies.

9.9
The Committee shall work and liaise as necessary with other Board 
committees, ensuring the interaction between committees and with the 
Board is reviewed regularly. 
 
• oversee any major changes in employee benefits structures throughout 
the Group; 
• agree the policy for authorising claims for expenses from the directors, 
• not authorise any payment or proposed payment to any existing, 
proposed or previous executive director or chairman that the 
Committee does not honestly and reasonably believe is consistent with 
the remuneration policy most recently approved by shareholders; 
• agree share ownership guidelines for executive directors; 
• give guidance to the executive management in setting the levels of 
remuneration for the Group; 
• address any appropriate structural changes that need to be made to 
the remuneration policy in light of changes to the relevant taxation 
legislation i.e., pensions taxation; 
• ensure that performance related elements of remuneration form a 
proportion of the total remuneration package; 
• work with the Company's Audit and Risk Committee in evaluating 
performance criteria; 
• use a consistent approach to performance measurement and explain in 
the remuneration report how this is achieved; 
•  ensure that variable and share-based remuneration is not payable unless 
the performance measurement governing is robust. The Committee 
shall also satisfy itself as to the accuracy of recorded performance 
measures that govern vesting of such remuneration; 
• determine the policy for, and scope of, pension arrangements for each 
executive director and other senior executives; 
• review and consider all executive and management compensation 
agreements to ensure that they are reasonable and in the best interests 
of the Group, taking into consideration the financial circumstances 
of the Group and to the extent required by stock exchange/market 
policies, ensure that the Board submits executive and management 
compensation arrangements for review and prior acceptance; 
• be aware of and oversee any major changes in employee benefit 
structures throughout the Group; and 
• work closely with the Nomination Committee in relation to the 
remuneration to be offered to any new executive director.

10.1
The Committee chair shall report to the Board after each meeting on the 
nature and content of its discussions, recommendations and actions to be 
taken.
10.2
The Committee shall make whatever recommendations to the Board it 
deems appropriate on any area within its remit where action or improvement 
is needed, and adequate time should be available for Board discussion when 
necessary.
10.3
The Committee shall provide a description of its work in the Company’s 
annual report in line with the requirements of the UK Corporate Governance 
Code, where it is appropriate.
10.4

information, as set out in The Companies (Directors’ Remuneration Policy 
and Directors’ Remuneration Report) Regulations 2019 and the UK Corporate 
Governance Code (so far as it is appropriate to do so) are fulfilled, and that a 
report on the directors' remuneration policy and practices is included in the 
Company’s annual report and put to shareholders for approval at the AGM as 
necessary.
10.5
If the Committee (or the Company) has appointed remuneration consultants 
to advise it, the annual report shall identify such consultants alongside a 
statement about any other connection the remuneration consultants have 
with the Company or any individual members of the Board.
